metadata.title: Automated CI/CD Pipeline & Cloud Deployment — Frontend Application
metadata.source: Fellow-supplied 8-slide narration script (CI/CD + containerized deployment overview), provided 2026-10-09. Continues medas-frontend-cicd, medas-ci-rollback and medas-trust-chain.
metadata.description: A consolidated walkthrough of the frontend's full CI/CD pipeline: the multi-stage Docker build, the Cloud Run + Artifact Registry infrastructure, Workload Identity Federation auth, automated PR gates and tag-triggered deploys, the one-click rollback workflow, and the environment-agnostic design that carries the same pipeline from dev through staging and production.
metadata.note: GitHub-dark skin for the six pipeline-mechanics beats (diegetic subject surface, GitHubCallChain diagrams per the supplied slide structure), Claude-cream skin for the INTRO bookend, the closing verdict card, and the OUTRO. Narration text is the fellow-supplied script verbatim; only the shot/visual design was authored here. Diagram-only per the source script -- no screen recordings.

beats.role_note: COLD OPEN LAW -- Claude cream skin, slide 1 title card
beats.narration_text: Today I'll walk through the CI/CD and deployment pipeline I built for the frontend application — covering how it's containerized, deployed to Google Cloud, secured, automated, and designed to roll back instantly if needed.

props.command: git tag v1.0.0 && git push origin v1.0.0
props.topic: DOCKER · ARTIFACT REGISTRY · CLOUD RUN · GITHUB ACTIONS
props.runningText: containerize → deploy → secure → automate → roll back…
output: frontend CI/CD on Google Cloud Run

beats.narration_text: The application is packaged using a multi-stage Docker build. The first stage compiles the React and Vite frontend into optimized static assets. Those assets are then handed to a lightweight Nginx stage, which serves the app. The result is a small, clean production image — no build tools, no source code, just the compiled app and a minimal web server configured to handle single-page-application routing correctly.

nodes.d: application source, not yet compiled
npm ci && npm run build → optimized static assets
lightweight image, serves the built assets only
no build tools, no source code — just the app + a minimal web server

props.caption: SPA routing lives in nginx.conf -- every unmatched path falls back to index.html.

beats.narration_text: That container image is stored in Google Cloud's Artifact Registry, where every build is version-tagged and kept as an immutable, traceable artifact. From there, it's deployed to Cloud Run — Google's fully managed serverless container platform, which handles scaling, load balancing, and HTTPS automatically, so there's no server infrastructure to manage.

nodes.d: built in the previous stage
every build stored, version-tagged and immutable
fully managed serverless containers — scaling, load balancing, HTTPS handled automatically

props.caption: No server infrastructure to manage -- Cloud Run owns that whole layer.

beats.narration_text: Rather than storing long-lived service account keys in GitHub — a common security risk — the pipeline uses Workload Identity Federation. This lets GitHub Actions authenticate to Google Cloud with short-lived, automatically rotated credentials, scoped through IAM so that only this specific repository can request access. It's a keyless, least-privilege security model.

nodes.d: the workflow run requesting access
short-lived, automatically rotated credentials — no stored key
scoped to exactly this repository — least privilege

props.caption: No long-lived service account key ever sits in GitHub -- that's the liability this design removes.

beats.narration_text: On the automation side, every pull request runs through quality gates automatically: linting, a full automated test suite, and a production build — before any code is merged. When a release is tagged, a separate pipeline takes over: it builds the application with the correct environment configuration, pushes the image to Artifact Registry, and deploys it straight to Cloud Run — a fully automated, zero-manual-steps release process.

nodes.d: every change, before merge
automated quality gates must pass first
the deploy trigger — a deliberate release decision
image built, pushed to Artifact Registry, deployed to Cloud Run — zero manual steps

props.caption: Merging and releasing are two separate decisions -- only a tag ships anything.

beats.narration_text: Because every build is stored as a versioned artifact, rolling back isn't a fire drill — it's a single action. A dedicated rollback workflow can redeploy any previously validated image instantly, without rebuilding anything. Build and deploy are fully decoupled, which means recovery is fast and low-risk.

nodes.d: already validated, already stored in Artifact Registry
a dedicated, separate action — no rebuild
the known-good version, live again

props.caption: Build and deploy are fully decoupled -- rolling back is a deployment operation, not an engineering fire drill.

beats.role_note: slide 7 -- dev / staging / production, same pipeline
beats.narration_text: The entire pipeline is environment-agnostic by design. The same workflows that power development deployments drive staging and production as well — differentiated only by release tag and environment configuration. That means the process already proven in development scales directly into staging and production without being rebuilt from scratch.

nodes.d: same workflow, dev tag + environment config
same workflow, staging tag + environment config
same workflow, production tag + environment config

props.caption: One proven pipeline, three environments -- only the tag and the GitHub Environment differ.

beats.role_note: slide 8 -- the verdict card, Claude cream skin
beats.narration_text: In short: a secure, fully automated deployment pipeline — containerized, cloud-native, and ready to extend into staging and production with confidence.

props.artifactHeading: Fully automated. Secure by design. Ready to scale.
artifactLines: Containerized: a two-stage Docker build ships nothing but the compiled app and Nginx.
Secure: Workload Identity Federation replaces stored keys with short-lived, scoped credentials.
Automated: PR quality gates, then a tag-triggered build-push-deploy with zero manual steps.
Resilient: a one-click rollback workflow redeploys any validated image instantly.
Scalable: the same pipeline drives dev, staging, and production — differentiated only by tag and environment.
